subject: Regional edge failover: APAC/US services reroute & follow-up
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>

Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 10:20:00 -0700
Subject: Regional edge failover: APAC/US services reroute & immediate guidance

Hi Amit —

We detected an API edge-level outage affecting a subset of our APAC and US public routing domains starting ~09:50 PDT. Your traffic to the impacted endpoints may see connection failures or timeouts. We have activated our edge failover policy to reroute requests to healthy regions (EU central) and started automated model fallbacks where needed.

What we have done for Acme (immediate):
- Enabled cross-region reroute for your org ID (route -> eu-central-1) so requests will be served from EU while the APAC/US edge heals.
- Applied the conservative model fallback (gpt-redwood-1 -> gpt-redwood-1-compact) for requests with max_latency <= 500ms to reduce token generation stalls.
- Temporarily increased concurrency limits on your dedicated pool to smooth bursts during reroute.

Recommended actions for your engineering team (simple, low-risk):
1) If you specify the region parameter in API calls, switch to region: eu-central-1 for the next 2–6 hours. Example: 
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY\" 
  -d '{"model":"gpt-redwood-1","region":"eu-central-1","input":"..."}'

2) If you rely on pinned model versions, consider allowing our compatible fallback model for up to 6 hours. This is already enabled for your account but you can opt out by hitting the account endpoint.
3) Implement client retry with exponential backoff for idempotent requests; prefer 2xx retries up to 3 attempts with jitter.

We estimate full re-routing normalization in ~90–180 minutes pending the cloud provider's network stabilization. I will send a formal post-incident note with timeline and RCA once we have confirmation from Cloud NOC and our infra team.

Attachments: acme-mitigation-checklist.pdf, edge-failover-steps.md

If you want, we can set up a quick 15-minute call to walk through the change and confirm your integration is stable — I have availability 11:00–11:30 PDT.

Thanks,
Soojin

Forwarding customer thread — quick internal notes:

On customer latency: This is expected during cross-region failover; EU nodes are healthy but cold-starts + longer RTTs cause p95 to spike. Suggested immediate mitigations:
- Increase token_limit for chat completions on account to reduce chunking (if safe).
- Enable short-term caching for repeated prefixes (ex: product-summary templates).
- We should surface a temporary policy that sets max_tokens shorter for non-critical calls.

Root cause (preliminary): CloudCorp announced a fiber flap in their us-east and ap-southeast peering clusters at 09:48 UTC which caused a partial withdrawal of some edge POPs. Our edge routing gracefully fallbacked but some sessions timed out before re-establishing.

Subject: Post-incident follow-up: timeline, mitigations, next steps (Acme)

Hi Amit —

Quick follow-up and summary now that the edge failover has stabilized for your traffic. Thank you for the patience and the heads-up about tail latency. Below is the post-incident summary specific to Acme plus recommended next steps.

Summary (what happened)
- 2026-06-15 09:48 PDT: Cloud Corp reported fiber peering instability affecting several edge POPs; some Redwood edge routers withdrew available routes.
- 09:50 PDT: Our monitoring triggered failover to eu-central-1 for affected endpoints. Automated model fallback engaged for latency-sensitive routes.
- 10:40 PDT: Majority of connections re-established; automated rollback started.
- 11:25 PDT: Edge routing fully normalized.

Impact to Acme:
- Failed requests peaked at ~3.8% of baseline during the 09:50–10:40 window.
- Temporary p95 increased to ~850ms for generation requests routed to EU.
- No customer request data was re-ordered; we do not perform opaque request replays — only idempotent retries at the client level will create duplicates.

Mitigations we applied for Acme:
- Cross-region reroute enabled for your org during the event.
- Conservative fallback model enabled to reduce stall risk.
- Short-term concurrency increase on your pool to avoid queuing.

Recommended follow-up actions for Acme engineering:
1) Keep client-side retry with idempotency keys enabled for any non-idempotent calls to avoid duplicate effects.
2) For latency-sensitive paths, reduce max_tokens by ~10–20% during cross-region operation and re-evaluate.
3) Enable prefix caching for repeated prompts; we can share a config snippet if helpful.

Next steps on our side:
- We will publish a full postmortem draft here: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2B3cPostmortemDraft (view-only) by EOD today.
- We are scheduling a 30-minute technical review with your team to confirm mitigations and any adjustments; proposed slots attached.
- Lauren will include a small goodwill credit for impacted request volume; Jonas has the list of qualifying customers and will confirm eligibility.

Attachments: 20260615-incident-timeline.csv, postmortem-draft.md

If you'd like the technical review now, reply with a preferred time and we'll lock it in.

Thanks again for the quick collaboration — we take these incidents seriously and will follow up with a finalized RCA.

Best,
Soojin
